model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five distinct gating configurations in a neural network architecture, as visualized through two line plots displayed in separate rows. The x-axis in both plots is labeled “Layer” and spans from 0 to 25, marked at intervals of 5, indicating a linear progression through the network’s depth. The left plot’s y-axis is labeled “Mass,” ranging from 0 to 400, while the right plot’s y-axis is labeled “Res. sink,” ranging from 0.0 to 0.2, both using linear scales. Row 1 (Baseline) shows a sharp increase in “Mass” after layer 6, peaking near layer 10 and again near layer 20, with corresponding spikes in “Res. sink” after layer 6. Row 2 (SDPA Gating) exhibits significantly lower “Mass” values across all layers, with no discernible peaks in “Res. sink.” Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) mirrors Row 2’s “Mass” profile but shows minor residual “Res. sink” activity after layer 6. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) display “Mass” patterns similar to the baseline, with pronounced peaks after layer 6 and elevated “Res. sink” values in the same regions. All plots use solid lines with no markers, and the visual trends are consistent with the caption’s description of activation and attention sink behavior under each gating scheme.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five distinct gating configurations, organized into five rows of subplots, each corresponding to a specific gating strategy. The x-axis across all subplots is labeled “Layer” and spans a linear range from 0 to approximately 25, with major tick marks at intervals of 5, representing sequential model layers. The y-axis in the left column of plots is labeled “Mass” and ranges from 0 to 400, with tick marks at intervals of 100, quantifying the magnitude of activations; the y-axis in the right column is labeled “Best token” and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2, indicating the normalized score or probability of the top-ranked token in attention mechanisms. Row 1 (Baseline) displays a red line with circular markers and a solid line style, showing near-zero mass up to layer 6, followed by sharp peaks exceeding 300 at layers 10, 15, and 20, and a corresponding “Best token” line that drops sharply near 0.0 after layer 6. Row 2 (SDPA Gating) features a green line with triangular markers and a solid line, maintaining low mass values (below 50) across all layers, with the “Best token” line remaining close to 1.0 throughout. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) shows a blue line with square markers and a solid line, exhibiting mass peaks similar to Row 2 (below 100) but with a “Best token” line that dips slightly below 0.8 around layer 15 before recovering. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) display a magenta line with diamond markers and a solid line, mirroring the sharp mass spikes and “Best token” collapse observed in Row 1, with mass values exceeding 300 at layers 10, 15, and 20, and the “Best token” line dropping below 0.2 after layer 6.
model_annotations.English: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five distinct gating configurations in a neural network, plotted as functions of layer index. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 25 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis on the left, labeled “Max,” ranges from 0 to 400 and quantifies the magnitude of activations, while the right y-axis, labeled “Rel. Attn.,” spans from 0.0 to 0.2 and measures relative attention sink strength. Row 1 (Baseline) displays a red line with circular markers and a solid style, showing near-zero activations until layer 6, followed by sharp spikes peaking above 350 at layers 10 and 20, accompanied by attention sinks rising to 0.2. Row 2 (SDPA Gating) shows a green line with square markers and a dashed style, maintaining low activations (<50) and no attention sinks (0.0) across all layers. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) mirrors Row 2’s activation profile with a blue line and triangle markers, but exhibits small residual attention sinks (~0.05) at layers 10 and 20. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) are represented by cyan and magenta lines with diamond and pentagon markers, respectively, both showing activation patterns and attention sinks that closely resemble Row 1, with peaks exceeding 300 and attention sinks reaching 0.15–0.2 at later layers.
model_annotations.German: Figure 6 presents a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a neural network, with each row corresponding to a distinct gating strategy and plotted against layer number. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans a linear scale from 0 to approximately 22, with tick marks at intervals of 5, representing the depth of the network’s layers. The y-axis on the left subplot, labeled “Max,” ranges from 0 to 400 and quantifies the maximum activation magnitude per layer, while the right subplot’s y-axis, labeled “Rel. max,” spans from 0.0 to 1.2 and represents a normalized or relative maximum activation value. In Row 1 (Baseline), a red line with triangular markers and a solid style shows near-zero activation until Layer 6, where it sharply rises to approximately 400 and remains high through Layer 22, with a small dip around Layer 18. Row 2 (SDPA Gating), depicted by a green line with circular markers and a solid style, remains near zero across all layers, indicating suppressed activations. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating), shown with a blue line and square markers, mirrors Row 2’s low activation profile but exhibits minor residual peaks around Layers 10 and 20, reaching approximately 50. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) replicate Row 1’s behavior: a red line with triangular markers rises sharply after Layer 6 to 400 and sustains high values, with a slight dip near Layer 18, while the corresponding right subplot for these rows shows a relative maximum that climbs to 1.2 after Layer 6 and remains elevated.
